title: Fill a lidded weekly pill organizer for Monday, Wednesday and Friday
instruction: put one tablet in each of the monday, wednesday and friday compartments and close their lids
context: Filling weekly pill organizers is a routine chore for older adults and their carers, and a dose in the wrong day, a double dose or a lid left open is a real medication error. The robot must read the day labels, flip open only the requested days' lids, put exactly one tablet in each, and snap the lids shut.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward is away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. (1) Pill organizer: blue plastic, fixed to the table, 35.4 cm wide, 6.8 cm deep, 2.3 cm tall; seven compartments in a row, each 4.6 cm wide and 6 cm deep inside, walls 4 mm thick and 2 cm tall on a 3 mm floor. Its compartments' near inside edge is 27 cm forward; it is centred left to right, Monday's compartment centre 15 cm left, then every 5 cm to Sunday's 15 cm right. Each compartment has its own lid: a light-blue plastic plate 6.8 cm deep, 4.8 cm wide and 2 mm thick (5 g), hinged along the top of the back wall, with a grip tab 2.5 cm long, 1.6 cm wide and 8 mm tall sticking out toward the arms from the middle of its front edge. The hinges are stiff (about 0.02 N m of friction), so a lid stays at whatever angle it is left; it opens to 150 degrees. All seven lids start closed. (2) Label strip: white card, 35.4 x 7 cm, flat on the table, its back edge 3 cm in front of the organizer's front wall, printed with matte black block capitals M T W T F S S (each 4 cm wide, 5.6 cm tall), each centred in front of its compartment, upright as seen from behind the arms. (3) Pill tray: a grey plastic block, 8 cm deep, 20 cm wide, 3 cm tall, fixed, centred 13 cm forward and left to right. (4) Tablets: three white caplets, 22 x 10 x 8 mm, 2 g each, lying flat on the tray with their long side pointing forward, centred 13 cm forward at 6 cm left, centred, and 6 cm right. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored once, after the episode ends, by counting the tablets in each compartment (a tablet counts if its centre is inside a compartment's walls, below their tops) and checking each lid (closed means open less than 10 degrees, i.e. its front edge less than 1.2 cm above the wall tops). 0.0 if any tablet is in Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday or Sunday (wrong day). Otherwise, for each of Monday, Wednesday and Friday holding exactly one tablet: 1/3 if its lid is closed, 1/6 if its lid was left open; the total is rounded to two decimals (0, 0.17, 0.33, 0.5, 0.67, 0.83 or 1.0). A day holding two or three tablets (a double dose) earns nothing. Tablets left on the tray, the table, the label strip, a lid or a wall top don't count. Other days' lids may be opened and left open without penalty. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Empty every compartment, close all seven lids, and put the three tablets back on the tray at their marked spots. The organizer, label strip and tray are fixed (tape or putty). Real 22 mm vitamin caplets or 3D-printed replicas both work; replace any that crack. A real organizer with snap lids works if its hinges are stiff enough to hold a lid open.
fidelity: Calibrated YAM station replica in Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Sim). The organizer is a rigid base welded to the table with seven rigid lids, each on a revolute joint with constant-torque (Coulomb) friction, so a lid holds any angle; real organizer lids also snap shut with a small latch, which is not modelled (closed is judged by angle only). The label strip and tray are fixed rigid boxes; the day letters are 1 mm raised black strips on the strip (printed in the real world). The tablets are rigid 22 x 10 x 8 mm boxes, not rounded caplets, so they slide and settle a little differently. Lighting and cameras follow the station calibration.
